corrections.notes: R50 User Manual v.25121 p.4 'R50 Hardware': 'Onboard Networking 2x 10 GbE / Additional Networking 1 (Optional) 2x 10/25/40/100 GbE / Additional Networking 2 (Optional) 2 or 6 x 100GBaseT or SR'. The high-speed pair is the fibre port: manual section 9.1 '10/40/100GbE NIC Cabling' tells the installer to seat SR4 optics, i.e. 4-lane parallel optics - QSFP28 for 100GBASE-SR4 and QSFP+ for 40GBASE-SR4. 40G and 100G physically cannot be carried by a single-lane SFP+/SFP28 cage, so the description's 'SFP+' is the wrong cage name (it should read QSFP28) and these two ports are modelled qsfp28. The datasheet's '10/25/40/100' is the card's whole speed family: 10G and 25G are QSFP28 breakout modes (4x10G / 4x25G) or QSA-adapter modes, not native port rates, so speedCaps are the cage-native 40/100G exactly as the rest of the catalogue models a QSFP28 port (cf. devices/cisco/n9k-c9336c-fx2.json, same [40000,100000] on 40/100G QSFP28). oobm is the dedicated out-of-band IPMI port and is copper 1GbE RJ-45 (R50 Basic Setup Guide v3.0 rear panel labels 'OOBM' separately from the '10Gb RJ-45 x2' onboard pair). Two caveats for a follow-up: (1) NONE of these port names match R50 enumeration - 'R-Series Network Port IDs' v.231101 p.6 lists the R50b/R50BM integrated ports as eno1/eno2 and the add-on high-speed pair as enp101s0f4/enp101s0f4d1, so enp1s0f0/enp1s0f1 is an R40-style pattern and should be renamed (not renamed here: this tool must not invent names); (2) the 10/25/40/100GbE pair is an add-in card - a base 3rd-gen R50 has 2x 10Gb RJ-45 onboard plus PCIe slots, which is why the datasheet headlines this pair as 'Additional Networking 1 (Optional)'. The copper 10GBase-T onboard pair is not modelled in this spec at all.

verification.detail: FortiADC 1000F QuickStart Device Guide labels 8x GE SFP ports 1-8, 8x GE RJ45 ports 9-16, 4x 10G SFP+ ports 17-20 and a dedicated 1G GE RJ45 MGMT port; datasheet FAD-1000F agrees (4x 10 GE SFP+, 8x GE SFP, 8x GE RJ45, 1x GE RJ45 mgmt). Spec matches port-for-port; only nit is speedCaps [100,1000] on the 1G SFP cages (100BASE-X is not a listed rate).

Cisco ASR 1001-X Hardware Installation Guide: six built-in 1 GE SFP-only interfaces (do not support SFP+) and two built-in 10 GE SFP+ interfaces, numbered 10GE 0/0/0-0/0/1 and GE 0/0/0-0/0/5 -> Gi0/0/0-5 = 1G SFP, Te0/0/0-1 = 10G SFP+ as specified. Nits: Te speedCaps include 1000 although Cisco says those ports are 10-GE rate only, and the file carries a stray 'Gi0' 1G interface that no Cisco numbering defines.

verification.device: cisco/ASR1001-X (devices/cisco/asr1001-x.json - duplicate of the model above)
verification.detail: This second file for the same model still models all eight built-in ports as 10G SFP+ with speedCaps [1000,10000]; the datasheet says six of them (Gi0/0/0-5) are 1 GE SFP-only cages, so a 10G optic on Gi0/0/2 must be refused. The duplicate model key means the catalogue holds both the fixed and the unfixed ASR 1001-X spec; one file needs deleting.

PA-1400 Series datasheet Table 3: PA-1420 I/O = 10/100/1000 (4), 1G/2.5G/5G (4), 1G/2.5G/5G PoE (4), 1G SFP (2), 1G/10G SFP/SFP+ (8); hardware reference confirms ports 13-14 = 1 Gbps SFP and ports 15-22 = 1 Gbps/10 Gbps SFP/SFP+ under one cage label 'SFP+ ports 13 through 22'. Spec matches exactly. Nits: speedCaps [100,1000] on 13-14 (cages are 1G) and the 10G HSCI port still has no connector, so it derives as RJ45 copper although it is an SFP+ cage.
